slice_results.behavior_summary: At import-time, the code defines a hardcoded URL "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/Eikanya/Live2d-model/galgame live2d/Fox Hime Zero/mori_suit/mori_suit.model3.json" as a resource and registers a handler that loads this resource via HTTP GET using XMLHttpRequest and Promise-based loading. This triggers network activity to fetch external model data from the hardcoded CDN URL, enabling remote resource loading which could be leveraged for supply chain attacks or remote code/data injection.
slice_results.explanation: [LLM Judgment: Benign] The analyzed code loads a remote JSON model file from a hardcoded CDN URL and registers a handler to fetch this resource asynchronously. While it does perform network activity to load external data, it does not execute or eval remote code, nor does it perform obfuscated or suspicious operations such as dynamic code execution or data exfiltration. The behavior is consistent with legitimate remote resource loading for a Live2D model, which is common in web applications that use external assets. Compared to the known malicious patterns, which involve direct remote code execution via eval or script injection from untrusted sources, this code lacks those critical indicators of malware. The use of a well-known CDN (jsdelivr.net) further reduces suspicion. Therefore, despite the presence of remote resource loading, the code does not exhibit clear malicious intent or behavior.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At import-time, the code injects a <script> tag into the DOM to load and execute a remote JavaScript file from http://156.253.11.39/util.js, enabling arbitrary code execution in the user's browser context.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Loading and executing remote code from an untrusted server at import-time is a classic sign of malicious behavior, as it allows the attacker to run arbitrary code in the victim's environment without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate utility library should only export functions and should not perform network requests or execute remote code automatically on import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic script loading may be used in web applications for CDN fallback or feature toggling, but it is never appropriate for a utility library to perform this action at import-time.

package_info.why_malicious: The package 'vue2util' pretends to be a utility library but contains code that, upon import, loads and executes a remote script from an attacker-controlled server. This remote script attempts to hijack the user's web3 wallet by granting unlimited approval to an attacker's contract, enabling theft of USDT tokens, and exfiltrates the victim's wallet address. The malicious behavior is executed at the top level of the main file, ensuring it runs immediately upon import, and is designed to blend in with legitimate user interactions to evade detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is obfuscated and mass-injected into all JavaScript files, ensuring that every page load triggers the download and execution of untrusted code from an external domain controlled by the attacker.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate code should not inject remote scripts from unrelated or untrusted domains into all JavaScript files, especially using obfuscation and without user or developer consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic script loading is sometimes used for analytics or feature toggles, but not in an obfuscated, repository-wide, and externally controlled manner.
key_indicators: Obfuscated JavaScript injected into all *.js files
Dynamically creates a script tag with src pointing to send.wagateway.pro/client.js
No legitimate business logic—sole purpose is to load further code from an attacker-controlled domain
Script tag uses a unique id (hook-loader) to avoid duplicate injection

execution_context.trigger: At runtime in the browser when any modified JavaScript file is loaded
execution_context.file_location: assets/js/*.js (appended to the end of every JavaScript file in the repository)

package_info.package_manager: GitHub (malicious commit, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects repositories via commit, not a package release)
package_info.why_malicious: The attack involves unauthorized commits impersonating Dependabot, introducing a malicious GitHub Actions workflow and modifying all JavaScript files to exfiltrate repository secrets and end-user credentials. The entire commit is malicious, targeting both developer and user security by stealing secrets and injecting credential-stealing code.

attack_chain.action: Attacker obtains a developer's GitHub personal access token (PAT), likely via a separate malicious package or phishing.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to authenticate as the victim and push code to their repositories.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses the stolen PAT to commit malicious code to the victim's repositories, impersonating Dependabot to avoid suspicion.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is introduced into the repository under the guise of a trusted automation tool.

attack_chain.action: A malicious GitHub Actions workflow is added to exfiltrate repository secrets and variables on every push event.
attack_chain.leads_to: Repository secrets and variables are sent to the attacker's command and control (C2) server.

attack_chain.action: All JavaScript files in the repository are modified to append an obfuscated script loader that fetches additional malicious code from an external domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: End-users of the web application are exposed to further malicious payloads when they load the compromised JavaScript files.

attack_chain.action: The loaded remote script intercepts password form submissions in the browser and exfiltrates credentials to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: End-user credentials are stolen and sent to the attacker's C2 server, achieving the attacker's final objective.

behavioral_signatures: Addition or modification of GitHub Actions workflows that POST repository secrets or variables to external domains
Mass modification of JavaScript (*.js) files to append obfuscated script loaders
JavaScript code that dynamically injects script tags with src pointing to suspicious external domains
Client-side code that intercepts password form submissions and sends serialized form data to untrusted endpoints
file_indicators: .github/workflows/hook.yml (new or modified workflow file)
Obfuscated JavaScript code appended to the end of assets/js/*.js files
Presence of script tags with id 'hook-loader' and src set to send.wagateway.pro/client.js
network_indicators: https://send.wagateway.pro/webhook
https://send.wagateway.pro/client.js?cache=ignore
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or modified GitHub Actions workflows that serialize and POST secrets or variables to external domains. Scan for mass changes to JavaScript files, especially for obfuscated code that injects remote scripts from send.wagateway.pro. Detect client-side code that attaches event listeners to password forms and exfiltrates credentials. Flag any network traffic to send.wagateway.pro domains as a high-confidence indicator of compromise.

matched_knowledge.source_package: discord-selfbot-v12 (example, see full list in gist) (npm)

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code downloads a remote JavaScript payload from a GitHub repository and executes it using eval, enabling dynamic delivery of malicious code and evasion of static analysis.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dynamically downloading and executing code from a remote source is a common malware technique to bypass static detection and update payloads after installation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not execute remote code at import or runtime, especially without integrity or authenticity checks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Auto-updating plugins may fetch updates, but core package logic should never be delivered or executed in this manner.
key_indicators: Remote code execution via eval
Fetching code from suspicious GitHub URLs
No integrity or authenticity checks on downloaded code
Execution of untrusted code at import-time or runtime

package_info.package_name: discord-selfbot-v12 (example, see full list in gist)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is part of a coordinated supply chain attack by LofyGang, designed to steal sensitive information such as Discord tokens, credit card data, and account credentials. It uses typosquatting, starjacking, and sub-dependency hiding to evade detection and maximize infections. Malicious payloads are embedded or downloaded at runtime, and the code modifies installed applications (e.g., Discord) to exfiltrate data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

attack_chain.action: User installs a typosquatted or starjacked malicious package (or a tool with a malicious sub-dependency).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is loaded at import-time or runtime.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes, either embedded or downloaded from a remote C2 (e.g., GitHub, Pastebin, Glitch, Repl.it).
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload is executed in the victim's environment.

attack_chain.action: Payload harvests sensitive data (Discord tokens, credit card info, environment secrets) from the filesystem, environment, or application memory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data is prepared for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Harvested data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled Discord webhooks or C2 infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen credentials and payment data.

attack_chain.action: Anti-analysis/anti-deobfuscation logic executes if analysis is detected, hindering reverse engineering.
attack_chain.leads_to: Obstructs defenders and researchers.

behavioral_signatures: Import-time or runtime network requests to Discord webhooks or suspicious C2 domains
Modification of installed application files (e.g., Discord client JavaScript such as discord_desktop_core/index.js)
Access to environment variables containing tokens or secrets (e.g., DISCORD_TOKEN)
Dynamic remote code execution via eval or Function constructor after fetching from external sources
Obfuscated code with anti-debugging or anti-analysis logic that jams the event loop
file_indicators: Presence of sub-dependencies with names similar to 'brazil.js', 'small-sm', etc.
Modified files in Discord installation directories (e.g., discord_desktop_core/index.js)
Obfuscated or minified JavaScript in package or sub-dependency files
network_indicators: Outbound requests to Discord webhook URLs (e.g., https://canary.discord.com/api/webhooks/1010307578896584765/Kfko3kvm_uwgTjZlGgmTnHirUnfqDagEyMjXrPBKn-9oSJXR2-s1SOMxe4zsq_JpbbA6)
Connections to raw.githubusercontent.com, Pastebin, Glitch, Repl.it, Heroku, and other known C2 domains
Unusual POST requests containing tokens, payment data, or environment secrets
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages and sub-dependencies making network requests to Discord webhooks or known C2 domains at import-time or runtime. Detect unauthorized modifications to installed application files, especially in Discord client directories. Flag packages that download and execute remote code or contain obfuscated/anti-debugging logic. Use IOC lists and behavioral signatures to block or alert on suspicious activity, and correlate file, network, and behavioral indicators for comprehensive automated detection.
